sections.h: The startup recruiting stack by stage

Series A and B (50+ hires): add structured assessments (HackerRank for engineering), and Deel once you hire across borders. Keep Noon running on the roles that need outbound sourcing; its flat plan does not grow with seats.

sections.h: What counts as an AI recruiting tool
p: An AI recruiting tool uses machine learning or large language models to do part of the hiring workflow: finding candidates, writing outreach, screening applicants, scheduling, taking interview notes or matching people to roles. The useful question is not 'does it use AI?' but 'which hours does it remove?'. Most products fall into six types:
list: Autonomous agents complete a whole job from a brief: find candidates, verify contacts, run outreach and book the interview. Example: Noon.
AI search replaces Boolean with plain English or a job description, but a recruiter still runs each search and the follow-up. Examples: Juicebox, hireEZ, SeekOut.

Interview intelligence records interviews and writes the notes. Examples: Metaview, BrightHire.

sections.h: How to choose an AI recruiting tool
p: Start from the bottleneck. If you do not have enough qualified candidates, or nobody has time to source, buy an autonomous agent: it removes the most hours. If you have too many applicants, buy conversational screening or structured assessments. If interviews are the slow part, buy interview intelligence and scheduling automation. If you are an enterprise with years of applicants in your ATS, a talent intelligence platform can rediscover them.

Then check three things: what the AI does without a human (the 'What the AI does' column above), how cost scales (per seat, per credit, per agent or flat), and whether it writes back to your ATS. A tool that needs a recruiter to drive every search saves minutes; one that completes the task saves headcount-sized time.

faq.q: What is the best AI recruiting assistant?
faq.a: Noon for teams that also need candidates found: its agent sources and contacts candidates by email and SMS and its AI Coordinator answers questions and books interviews. Paradox is the best assistant for inbound hourly applicants.

faq.q: What does an AI recruiting assistant do?
faq.a: Answers candidate questions, screens with knockout questions, schedules interviews, writes interview notes and drafts outreach, depending on the product.

faq.q: Is LinkedIn Hiring Assistant worth it?
faq.a: If your candidates are only reachable on LinkedIn and you already pay for Recruiter, it speeds up searching and InMail drafting. It works only within LinkedIn's network and InMail credits; Noon searches beyond LinkedIn and contacts candidates by email and SMS.
